correctness.rationale: The computable paired product tree has path set exactly the Cartesian product of the factor path sets. Every product path computes both coordinate paths; factor leastness therefore makes the finite join a lower bound on every product-path degree, and the paired distinguished paths realize that degree. The categoricity corollary uses only the corrected two-way characterization for strong degrees on the cone above the double jump.

originality.rationale: The 2022/2024 source introduces and characterizes treeable degrees but does not state finite-join closure or the derived upper-cone join closure for strong degrees of categoricity. Targeted literature searches and repeated semantic overlap searches found no equivalent or stronger theorem. This remains a best-of-knowledge assessment.

value.rationale: The result supplies an upper-semilattice closure law for a recently isolated degree class and immediately yields a structural closure theorem for strong degrees of categoricity on the classified cone, while exposing the precise nonuniformity obstruction to an automatic countable-join extension.
